questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: Pseudo strabismus is described in the book as:
opts: A true latent deviation that appears on cover testing
An apparent deviation without true ocular misalignment
A paralytic deviation with limitation of movement
A restrictive deviation with positive forced duction
questions.exp: Pseudo strabismus = apparent deviation. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: Fill up: In the book's flowchart, pseudo strabismus has 2 types — pseudo eso and pseudo ___.
questions.exp: 2 types: Pseudo eso, Pseudo exo. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: All of the following are listed as causes of pseudo esotropia in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pseudo eso causes: Telecanthus, Epicanthus, Myopia; Hypertelorism causes pseudo exo. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: Match the pseudo eso cause with its mechanism per the book — 1) Telecanthus 2) Epicanthus 3) Myopia … A) Refractive cause of apparent eso B) Extra congenital medial fold upper to lower eyelid C) Increased ICD with normal IPD
questions.exp: Telecanthus: ↑ ICD + normal IPD; Epicanthus: extra congenital fold connecting upper to lower eyelid in medial part; Myopia is listed as third cause. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: Which statement about telecanthus and epicanthus is TRUE per the book?
opts: Telecanthus shows increased IPD with normal ICD
Epicanthus is an acquired lateral fold after trauma
Telecanthus shows increased ICD with normal IPD, epicanthus is a congenital medial fold upper to lower lid
Both telecanthus and epicanthus increase both ICD and IPD
questions.exp: Telecanthus: ↑ ICD + normal IPD; Epicanthus: an extra (congenital) fold of skin connecting upper eyelid to lower eyelid in the medial part. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Pseudo strabismus — apparent deviation and pseudo eso
questions.q: A 4-year-old with broad nasal bridge, medial canthi appear far apart but Pilla's pupillary distance measured is normal, no true deviation on Hirschberg. The book would label this as:
questions.exp: ↑ ICD + normal IPD = Telecanthus → pseudo eso. (Book p66)

questions.q: All of the following are listed as causes of pseudo exotropia in the book EXCEPT:
opts: ROP with temporal displacement of macula
questions.exp: Pseudo exo: Hypertelorism, ROP (temporal displaced macula), Hypermetropia; Epicanthus causes pseudo eso. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: Hypertelorism causing pseudo exo shows increased ICD and increased IPD due to ____ set orbits.
questions.exp: Hypertelorism: Increased ICD, Increased IPD (d/t wide set orbits). (Book p66)

questions.q: Match pseudo exo cause with mechanism — 1) Hypertelorism 2) ROP 3) Hypermetropia … A) Temporal displacement of macula B) Wide set orbits ↑ICD & IPD C) Refractive cause listed for pseudo exo
questions.exp: Hypertelorism = wide set orbits ↑ICD+IPD; ROP = D/t temporal displacement of macula; Hypermetropia = third listed cause of pseudo exo. (Book p66)

questions.q: A preterm infant with treated ROP now has macula dragged temporally, parents think child has outward deviation but cover test is orthotropic. Per the book this is:
opts: Pseudo exotropia from ROP due to temporal displacement of macula
questions.exp: ROP (Retinopathy of prematurity) D/t temporal displacement of macula → pseudo exo. (Book p66)

questions.q: Myasthenia gravis in the book is most common in:
questions.exp: Myasthenia gravis: m/c in young females. (Book p66)

questions.q: Which statement about myasthenia gravis pathology is TRUE per the book?
opts: Increased Ach receptors with morning worsening
Reduced Ach receptors with fatigue worsening in evening (m/c feature)
Antibodies against muscle fiber actin causing morning improvement
Increased muscarinic receptors with fixed weakness
questions.exp: Pathology: Reduced Ach receptors; Fatigue: Worsens in the evening (m/c feature). (Book p66)

questions.sec: Ocular Myopathies — myasthenia gravis ocular features
questions.q: All of the following are listed as ocular features of myasthenia gravis EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Ocular features: Ptosis B/L, Diplopia, Cogan lid twitch sign, Orbicularis oculi weakness; miosis/enophthalmos is Horner's. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Ocular Myopathies — myasthenia gravis ocular features
questions.q: Fill up: Cogan lid twitch sign is upshoot of eyelid when changing gaze from down to ___.
questions.exp: Cogan lid twitch sign: Upshoot of eyelid when changing gaze from down to up. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Ocular Myopathies — myasthenia gravis ocular features
questions.q: A 24-year-old woman complains of drooping of both upper lids that worsens by evening, diplopia, and on asking her to look down then up, her lid overshoots. Forced opening of closed eyelids is easy. The book's sign described is:
opts: Cogan lid twitch sign with orbicularis oculi weakness
questions.exp: Cogan lid twitch: upshoot down→up; Orbicularis oculi weakness tested by forced opening of closed eyelids; B/L ptosis + diplopia + evening fatigue = myasthenia. (Book p66)

questions.q: Tensilon test for myasthenia gravis uses:
opts: Inj 0.2 mg of edrophonium (Anticholinesterase agent) → ↑ Ach
questions.exp: Diagnosis: Tensilon test: Inj 0.2 mg of edrophonium (Anticholinesterase agent) → ↑ Ach. (Book p67)

questions.q: In the book's Tensilon test photos, after injection there is:
questions.exp: Before injection ptosis, After injection → Improvement of ptosis. (Book p67)

questions.q: Fill up: Ice-pack test for myasthenia ptosis uses ice pack application for ___ mins → ptosis improvement.
questions.exp: Ice pack test: Ice pack application for 5 mins → Ptosis improvement. (Book p67)

questions.q: Match the test with its principle/result — 1) Tensilon test 2) Ice-pack test … A) Cold improves neuromuscular transmission → ptosis improves after 5 min ice B) Anticholinesterase ↑ Ach → ptosis improves after 0.2 mg edrophonium C) Sympathomimetic ↑ IPD
questions.exp: Tensilon: Inj 0.2 mg edrophonium (Anticholinesterase) → ↑ Ach → improvement; Ice-pack: 5 mins application → improvement. (Book p67)

questions.q: A bedside test that avoids injection and uses 5 minutes of cold application to show improvement in ptosis, as per the book's second photo series, is:
questions.exp: Ice-pack test: Ptosis → Ice pack 5 mins → Ptosis improvement. (Book p67)

units.title: Pseudo strabismus — pseudo eso
units.guide: Pseudo strabismus = apparent deviation. 2 types: pseudo eso, pseudo exo. Pseudo eso causes: 1. Telecanthus: ↑ ICD + normal IPD. 2. Epicanthus: extra congenital fold of skin connecting upper eyelid to lower eyelid in medial part. 3. Myopia. Pseudostrabismus photo labels TELECANTHUS.

units.title: Pseudo exo and myasthenia gravis features
units.guide: Pseudo exo causes: 1. Hypertelorism: Increased ICD, Increased IPD (d/t wide set orbits). 2. ROP (Retinopathy of prematurity) D/t temporal displacement of macula. 3. Hypermetropia. Myasthenia gravis: m/c in young females. Pathology: Reduced Ach receptors. Fatigue worsens in evening (m/c feature). Ocular: Ptosis B/L, Diplopia, Cogan lid twitch sign (upshoot of eyelid when changing gaze from down to up), Orbicularis oculi weakness tested by forced opening of closed eyelids.

units.title: Myasthenia diagnosis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
units.guide: Diagnosis: Tensilon test: Inj 0.2 mg edrophonium (Anticholinesterase agent) → ↑ Ach. Before injection ptosis, after → improvement. Ice-pack test: Ptosis → ice pack application for 5 mins → ptosis improvement. Photo series shows B/L ptosis before, improved after.
